b1-razaclasepoder-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Castas in a Museum
b1-razaclasepoder-01.scenario: You are Meg. You visited a museum exhibition about casta paintings, and Carlos asks what you learned.
b1-razaclasepoder-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how people were classified in the 18th century.
cues: Say that people were classified by their origin
Say where the classification was written down
Say what many historians think about daily life
b1-razaclasepoder-01.target: Se clasificaba a las personas según su origen, y se anotaba en los registros. Los historiadores dicen que la vida diaria era diferente.
b1-razaclasepoder-01.english: People were classified according to their origin, and it was written in the registers. Historians say daily life was different.
b1-razaclasepoder-01.canDo: I can explain how people were classified in colonial cities.

b1-razaclasepoder-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Bourbon Reforms
b1-razaclasepoder-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You read a book about the Bourbon reforms, and Meg asks why the criollos were upset.
b1-razaclasepoder-02.prompt: Tell Meg why the criollos were upset.
cues: Say why, with a formal connector
Say what happened to the Jesuits in 1767
b1-razaclasepoder-02.target: Los criollos perdieron cargos debido a la llegada de más peninsulares. En 1767 el rey expulsó a los jesuitas.
b1-razaclasepoder-02.english: The criollos lost posts because of the arrival of more peninsulares. In 1767 the king expelled the Jesuits.
b1-razaclasepoder-02.canDo: I can explain why many criollos lost posts and felt resentful after the Bourbon reforms.

b1-razaclasepoder-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Túpac Amaru II
b1-razaclasepoder-03.scenario: You are Meg. You watched a documentary about Túpac Amaru II, and Carlos asks what you remember.
b1-razaclasepoder-03.prompt: Tell Carlos about the rebellion of 1780.
cues: Say what happened to him in 1781
Say that people remembered him despite the defeat
b1-razaclasepoder-03.target: Un cacique, José Gabriel Condorcanqui, dirigió una rebelión en 1780. Lo ejecutaron en Cuzco en 1781, pero a pesar de la derrota muchas personas lo recordaron.
b1-razaclasepoder-03.english: A cacique, José Gabriel Condorcanqui, led a rebellion in 1780. He was executed in Cuzco in 1781, but despite the defeat many people remembered him.
b1-razaclasepoder-03.canDo: I can say who Túpac Amaru II was and what happened in 1780 and 1781.

b1-razaclasepoder-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Gracias al sacar
b1-razaclasepoder-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You read a book about colonial society, and Meg asks about the gracias al sacar.
b1-razaclasepoder-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the gracias al sacar was and what it shows.
cues: Say that in 1795 a decree let people buy a change of status
Say what is important for historians today
b1-razaclasepoder-04.target: En 1795 una cédula permitió comprar un cambio de condición. Para muchos historiadores es importante que hoy se entienda esta historia.
b1-razaclasepoder-04.english: In 1795 a decree allowed people to buy a change of status. For many historians it is important that this history is understood today.
b1-razaclasepoder-04.canDo: I can explain what the gracias al sacar was.

b1-razaclasepoder-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Colonial Legacies
b1-razaclasepoder-05.scenario: You are Meg. You had a class about independence, and Carlos asks whether things changed afterwards.
b1-razaclasepoder-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what changed and what did not.
cues: Say what the law was like before
Say what has changed since then
b1-razaclasepoder-05.target: Antes las personas tenían menos derechos, y desde entonces la ley ha cambiado. Pero la desigualdad no ha desaparecido.
b1-razaclasepoder-05.english: Before, people had fewer rights, and since then the law has changed. But inequality has not disappeared.
b1-razaclasepoder-05.canDo: I can explain what changed in the law and what has not disappeared since independence.

b1-razaclasepoder-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Race, Class and Power
b1-razaclasepoder-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You visited a museum about colonial society with a friend, and Meg asks what you learned.
b1-razaclasepoder-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one thing about castas and one about independence.
cues: Say what happened to the castas after independence
b1-razaclasepoder-consolidation.target: En el siglo XVIII se clasificaba a las personas según su origen. Después de la independencia, en varios países se abolieron las castas.
b1-razaclasepoder-consolidation.english: In the 18th century people were classified according to their origin. After independence, the castas were abolished in several countries.
b1-razaclasepoder-consolidation.canDo: I can explain how people were classified in colonial cities and what changed under the Bourbon reforms.
